correctness.rationale: The four lines in general position are projectively equivalent over C to x=0, y=0, z=0, x+y+z=0. Recomputing the complete quadrangle by cross products gives six distinct base points and three distinct diagonal intersections off the base locus; common blown-up points of distinct lines separate into distinct direction points on the exceptional curve. The thirteen listed curves are all negative curves: −K=H+(sum R_i)/2 is nef, adjunction forces negative irreducible curves into (self-intersection, anticanonical degree)=(−1,1) or (−2,0), and Cauchy in the plane multiplicities gives degree at most two. Each five-element subset of the base points contains an original collinear triple, excluding the conic possibility. The incidence graph is connected with 21 nodes and thirteen rational components whose valencies are three or four, hence stable of genus nine. Over Q and in characteristics 7 and 13 the stated decomposition follows from QQᵗ=2I+J, PPᵗ=2I and QPᵗ=J: on the edge space the images of zero-sum vertex and matching spaces are orthogonal and have nondegenerate forms, and the constant line splits off (dimension six altogether). The constant block has rank two over both finite fields, the repeated vertex block has determinant seven, and the repeated matching block determinant thirteen. Hence the reduced nullities are three and two, exhausting the determinant valuations and forcing elementary primary groups. Fresh exact Smith reductions at two roots independently yield 1^9,7,91,91, determinant 57967, and the asserted polynomial. The Néron statement is valid under the specified regular split unit-thickness hypothesis; no fibration on X is inferred.
residual_risks: The verification concerns the full reduced boundary over C and does not extend to arbitrary arithmetic descent or weighted nodes.

value.rationale: This is the whole canonical negative-curve boundary of a geometrically distinguished singular cubic resolution, not a selected induced subgraph. Its integral component group is an exact invariant a user of this genus-nine degeneration can need; the two local ranks prove that all 7- and 13-primary factors are elementary, which the spanning-tree count alone cannot do. The rational and prime-local block argument also explains where the two primary parts come from. Neither a known chamber support count nor the Picard torus of the singular nine-line divisor substitutes for this result.
residual_risks: Application to Néron models is conditional; there is no claim that this divisor is a fiber on the resolved surface.
